subject: Execution locus and subprocessor handoff questions — HappyMed prospect
messages:
From: Elisa Peterson <elisa.peterson@happymed.com>

Cc: Legal Ops <legalops@happymed.com>, Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@happymed.com>

Subject: Quick Q: where does data get executed / any cross-border hops?

Hi Stephanie,

I'm working through HappyMed's procurement security checklist and have a couple of focused questions about Redwood's runtime for inference and subprocessor hops:

- For the hosted API (we are investigating both hosted and Dedicated), where are inference requests executed (region level)? Do you have a map of the processing sites and which subprocessors are involved?
- In a typical request flow from a US-based client, do tokens or payloads ever leave the US (e.g., processed or cached in EU/APAC CDNs or edge nodes)?
- If cross-border handoffs happen, can you describe what moves, who controls keys, and whether we can restrict execution to a region or require on-prem/Dedicated only?
- Retention & deletion: who is responsible for deleting request-level telemetry and cache (Redwood or subprocessor) and what are typical SLA windows?

Procurement asked for an evidence pack we can attach (processing map, subprocessors inventory, and any attestation language). Could you point me to the right artifacts or send a short Q&A? We're on a tight timeline for our vendor review.

Thanks — Elisa
Elisa Peterson
Sr. Security Manager, HappyMed
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Elisa Peterson <elisa.peterson@happymed.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-11-22T09:42:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quick Q: where does data get executed / any cross-border hops?

Hi Elisa — thanks for the clear list. High level answers below; I'll attach an evidence package in a follow-up from our Security/Trust team.

- Execution loci: For our Hosted API, inference execution is pinned to the cloud region you select at request time (we default to us-west-2 for US tenants). We also publish a processing topology map showing inference pods, persistent KV cache locations, and edge cache nodes.
- Cross-border hops: Payloads may be temporarily routed through CDN edges for streaming or caching, but token-level inference is executed in the selected region. We do use global routing for control-plane telemetry (metrics/traces) — these are pseudonymized and aggregated for ops.
- Keys & control: Customer data used for inference is encrypted in transit (TLS) and at rest. KMS keys for tenant metadata are customer-scoped in Dedicated/Private deployments; for Hosted tenants we use customer-specific envelope keys backed by AWS KMS in the selected region.
- Deletion & SLA: We delete request-level temporary caches within 24 hours by default; customers can request stricter TTLs or retention windows (e.g., 0h) for Dedicated/Private. For proof, we'll include our deletion flow diagram and the subprocessor RL.

I've looped in Ben and Marissa to prepare the processing map + subprocessor inventory and a short narrative describing exactly what hops happen (CDN vs. execution). One quick question for procurement: are you evaluating Hosted or Dedicated as your primary control requirement? If Dedicated, we can provide region-pinned attestations and additional key control language.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-11-22T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Internal: technical summary for HappyMed evidence pack

Steph — drafting the tech answers for Marissa. Notes below that we'll include in the packet:

1) Execution path (hosted default):
   - Client -> Redwood API gateway (regional endpoint) -> Routing layer -> Inference pod in selected region (e.g., us-west-2).
   - KV/prefix cache: colocated in same region where feasible. We run an additional distributed read-through cache (FastCache) with optional EU edge nodes for low-latency reads — those are only for cached prefix tokens and do not run inference computation.

2) Subprocessors & control plane:
   - Primary compute: AWS in region (EC2/GPU instances).
   - Object storage for model artifacts: AWS S3 (replication configured per model policy).
   - Edge CDN: FastCache Inc. (CDN) with PoPs globally — used for streaming responses and static assets.
   - Telemetry/observability: Datadog for metrics (ingest aggregated in EU/US based on account region), logs stored in customer-scoped buckets with retention controls.

3) Cross-border specifics:
   - For Hosted tenants: model inference is region-pinned; cached fragments may be propagated to edge PoPs outside the region for performance. No raw request payloads are routed to third-party compute outside the execution region.
   - For Dedicated/Private: we can provide strict region pinning (no edge caching outside selected region) and customer-managed KMS.

4) Deletion:
   - Ephemeral caches: TTL default 24h (configurable).
   - Request logs: retained 90 days by default for troubleshooting; can be shortened for Dedicated/Private.
   - Deletion path: request -> control plane instructs storage/subprocessor to delete -> deletion event logged + audit record with timestamp. We aim for 7 days to fully purge objects across backups and replicated stores; we provide SLA language on Dedicated.

I recommend attaching: redwood_processing_map_v2.pdf (diagram), subprocessor_inventory_20271122.csv, and a short one-page note on deletion SLAs. Marissa — can you assemble and send?

- Ben
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi Elisa — forwarded with the assets Ben and I prepared. Please find the attached evidence pack and a short narrative below.

Attachment stubs:
- redwood_processing_map_v2.pdf (PDF, 2 pages) — visual of request hop: gateway -> regional inference -> KV cache -> optional edge cache.
- subprocessor_inventory_20271122.csv (CSV, 36 rows) — vendor roster, region of operation, role (compute/storage/cdn/observability).
- happy_med_evidence_request.xlsx (XLSX, 3 sheets) — answers to your procurement checklist with references and dates.

Short narrative (tl;dr):
- For Hosted accounts we execute inference in the region selected at account creation. Edge caches (for streaming/latency) may be outside the execution region but do not perform inference.
- Data in transit is encrypted. For Hosted we manage envelope keys in the selected AWS region; for Dedicated/Private we support customer-side KMS and on-prem key stores.
- Deletion: ephemeral caches expire by TTL (default 24h), request logs are retained 90 days by default; Dedicated customers can request shorter retention and we provide contractual SLA for 7-day purge across replicated objects.

If you want, we can:
- Produce a short attestation letter confirming region-pinning for Hosted (account-scoped) or Dedicated (contractual).
- Schedule a 30-minute technical call with Ben to walk through the processing map and any export-control questions.
